verses.28:2: {Afferte} ao Senhor glória e honra, {afferte} ao Senhor {nomini}: * adorai o Senhor {atrio}.
verses.28:3: {v3a} as águas, o Deus da majestade trovejou: * {v3b} muitas águas.
verses.28:4: A voz do Senhor {virtute}: * a voz do Senhor {magnificentia}.
verses.28:5: A voz do Senhor {p5} os cedros: * e o Senhor {confringet} os cedros do Líbano:
verses.28:6: E os {comminuet} {vitulum} do Líbano: * e {dilectus}, como um filho de unicórnios.
verses.28:7: A voz do Senhor {p7a} a chama de fogo: * a voz do Senhor {p7b} o deserto: e o Senhor abalará o deserto de Cades.
verses.28:9: A voz do Senhor {p9} {cervos}, e {revelabit} {condensa}: * e no seu templo todos {dicent}.
verses.28:10: O Senhor {diluvium}: * e o Senhor {sedebit} para sempre.
verses.28:11: O Senhor dará {virtutem} ao seu povo: * o Senhor {benedicet} o seu povo em paz.

decisions.why: afférre: 'bring to' (ἐνέγκατε ×4). Four times in two verses, and the thing brought changes — first the offerers' young rams (28:1b), then glory and honour (28:2): one verb carries both, so one Portuguese verb must too. 'trazer' is afférre's own sense and carries both objects; 'oferecer' is offérre's (65:15 'ófferam tibi', grep) and would merge two verbs; 'render' fits glory but not rams. The same formula returns in 95:7 ('Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus', grep) — formula row proposed. 'Trazei' is safe at the vós imperative (past 'trouxe'). Douay-Rheims 'Bring to the Lord' ×4; Matos Soares 1932 splits: 'Oferecei' (28:1), 'Rendei' (28:2).

options.label: Trazei
options.note: Ruling: afférre's sense; one verb for rams and glory, as the Latin.

options.label: Rendei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (28:2): fits glory, not the rams.

decisions.why: The Latin tells the two 'sons' apart by case: 'fílii Dei' is vocative (those addressed), 'fílios aríetum' accusative (what they bring). Portuguese has no case, and the two cola are built alike, so without a mark the ear takes 'filhos de Deus' as a second thing brought ('bring the sons of God to the Lord'). The vocative particle 'ó' supplies what the Latin ending does (grammar, D2) — both Vulgate-family versions have it (Douay-Rheims 'O ye children of God'; Matos Soares 1932 'ó filhos de Deus'). The glossary's 'vocative without ó unless the Latin has o' is written for 'Senhor', whose vocative nothing can mistake. 'fílii Dei' only here (grep).

options.label: ó filhos de Deus
options.note: Ruling: the vocative marked, as the Latin's case marks it.

options.label: filhos de Deus
options.note: Bare vocative (the glossary's habit for 'Senhor'); heard as a second object.

decisions.why: 'the sons of rams' (υἱοὺς κριῶν): the young rams brought as offerings — a line the Latin has with the Greek and the Hebrew lacks (the Hebrew doubles 'sons of God', בני אלים). The psalm plays on 'sons' three times: fílii Dei, fílios aríetum, fílius unicórnium (28:6). 'filhos de carneiros' keeps the word and the play; 'crias' is the plainer word for an animal's young and would break it; Matos Soares 1932 explains ('tenros cordeiros'), which D2 refuses. aríes → carneiro (the ram; 65:15, 113:4, 113:6 follow). Douay-Rheims 'the offspring of rams'.

options.label: filhos de carneiros
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word, and the psalm's 'sons' three times.

options.label: crias de carneiros
options.note: The plainer word for an animal's young; the play on 'filhos' lost.

decisions.why: Two datives in one colon: to the Lord, glory for his name (δόξαν ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ). 'ao Senhor … ao seu nome' stacks two 'ao' and makes the name a second recipient; 'para o seu nome' keeps the dative's sense (glory destined for the name) and the colon clear. 'a glória do seu nome' (a genitive) says another thing. The Monday Lauds antiphon joins 28:3 to this colon: 'Deus majestátis * intónuit: afférte glóriam nómini ejus' (Psalmi major.txt, Day1 Laudes1, grep) — 'trazei glória para o seu nome' serves it.

options.label: glória para o seu nome
options.note: Ruling: the dative's sense, without two 'ao'.

options.label: glória ao seu nome
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'glory to his name': the preposition to the letter.

options.label: a glória devida ao seu nome

forms.nomini: a glória devida ao seu nome

decisions.latin: adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus
decisions.why: átrium → átrio (glossary, working; the blind reader of Ps 133 did not know it). The same colon closes 95:8 word for word (grep) — formula row proposed. The adjective after the noun, as 'monte santo' (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'in his holy court'; Matos Soares 1932 'no átrio do seu santuário' (makes the adjective a noun). 'adorai' is safe (past 'adorei').

decisions.latin: Vox Dómini super aquas … Dóminus super aquas multas
decisions.why: The seven 'Vox Dómini' of the psalm (28:3, 4 ×2, 5, 7 ×2, 9) are all acclamations without a finite verb: a noun, then a place (28:3, 4) or a participle (28:5, 7, 9). They are kept so — 'A voz do Senhor' identical seven times, each time a noun phrase — because the repetition, shaped alike, is the psalm. A copula is what D2 allows and both Vulgate-family versions supply ('The voice of the Lord is upon the waters'; 'A voz do Senhor está sobre as águas'); it is the option. 28:3's middle colon has the one finite verb ('o Deus da majestade trovejou'), which stands out as the Latin's does.

options.label: A voz do Senhor sobre … o Senhor sobre
options.note: Ruling: the acclamation, verbless as the Latin.

options.label: A voz do Senhor está sobre … o Senhor está sobre

forms.v3a: A voz do Senhor está sobre

decisions.latin: Vox Dómini in virtúte: * vox Dómini in magnificéntia
decisions.why: 'in' of manner (ἐν ἰσχύι … ἐν μεγαλοπρεπείᾳ): the voice comes with power, with magnificence. 'com' says it; 'em poder' is heard as 'in office'. Verbless, as 28:3 (decision verbless). virtus of God → poder (glossary; 28:11 has the same noun). Matos Soares 1932 turns both nouns into adjectives ('é poderosa … é majestosa'); Douay-Rheims 'is in power … in magnificence'.

options.label: com poder … com magnificência
options.note: Ruling: the nouns kept, the preposition of manner.

options.label: é poderosa … é magnífica
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's build: the nouns become adjectives.

decisions.why: magnificéntia → magnificência (glossary, open; the row names 28:4; μεγαλοπρέπεια). The Ps 8 blind reader listed it as a word churchgoers may not know. 'majestade' is majéstas's, one verse before (28:3 'Deus majestátis'): the psalm would say one word for two.

options.label: majestade
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's sense ('majestosa'): majéstas's word in 28:3.

decisions.latin: Vox Dómini confringéntis … intercidéntis … concutiéntis … præparántis
decisions.why: The participles are genitive: they agree with 'Dómini', not with 'vox' — 'the voice of the Lord who breaks the cedars'. A relative clause keeps the noun phrase (decision verbless) and the Portuguese 'que' may be heard with either noun, which leaves the Latin's link to the Lord audible without shutting out the voice. Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 make the voice the subject of a finite verb ('The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars'), which changes the grammar's subject from the Lord to the voice; it is the option.

options.label: que quebra … que divide … que abala … que prepara
options.note: Ruling: relative clauses; the acclamation stays a noun phrase.

options.label: quebra … divide … abala … prepara
options.note: Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932: the voice as subject.

decisions.why: confríngere → quebrar (glossary, open; 2:9, 17:39). The participle and the future of one verb, the voice breaking and the Lord who will break: one Portuguese verb, 'quebra … quebrará'. 'despedaçar' carries the con- and is the glossary's option; it would crowd commínuet in 28:6 (→ esmigalhar).

commínuere → esmigalhar (glossary, open; 17:43 'E eu os esmigalharei como o pó'; λεπτυνεῖ, 'grind small'). Only these two places (grep). 'eas' are the cedars (cedrus is feminine in Latin): masculine 'os' in Portuguese. Matos Soares 1932 'os fará em pequenos pedaços'; Douay-Rheims 'reduce them to pieces'.

'vítulum' is accusative: the calf is compared as a thing crushed ('he will crush them as [he crushes] a calf of Lebanon'), not as one who crushes. Portuguese marks that with 'a' before the compared object ('como a um'), as Matos Soares 1932 does. The sense of the image is obscure in Latin and Greek alike (ὡς τὸν μόσχον τὸν Λίβανον); it is not explained. vítulus → bezerro (glossary; 28:6 named).

options.label: como um bezerro
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'as a calf': the case not heard.

decisions.why: 'and the beloved, like a son of unicorns' (ὁ ἠγαπημένος ὡς υἱὸς μονοκερώτων) — a Septuagintal line (the Hebrew has 'Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox'); the Latin names no one and has no verb, and neither is supplied: who the beloved is stays open (Matos Soares 1932's note reads Israel; not followed). diléctus only here as a substantive (grep 'dilectus'). 'o amado' is plain; 'o bem-amado' is the old devotional form. unicórnis → unicórnio (glossary). fílius kept (decision arietum: the psalm's third 'filho').

intercídere: 'cut asunder, divide, cut through' (L&S, citing this verse; διακόπτοντος). The lightning that splits the flame into forks. 'dividir' is Douay-Rheims's word and cannot be heard as putting the fire out, which 'cortar a chama' can; 'fender' is exact but literary. Matos Soares 1932 'despede chamas' is the Hebrew's sense ('hews out flames'). Only here (grep). flamma ignis → a chama de fogo (the Latin's singular).

options.label: corta
options.note: Plainer; may be heard as putting the flame out.

decisions.latin: concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades
decisions.why: Two Latin verbs, one Greek verb (συσσείοντος … συσσείσει): D15's test lets them be one Portuguese verb, and the verse then has the same shape as 28:5 (the voice that breaks, the Lord who will break; the voice that shakes, the Lord who will shake). commovéri → ser abalado is the glossary's (the movéri row; 14:5b, 20:8), so the active is 'abalar'. Douay-Rheims 'shaketh … shall shake'; Matos Soares 1932 'abala … fará tremer'.

options.label: abala … abalará
options.note: Ruling: one Greek verb, one Portuguese verb (commovébit → abalará).

decisions.why: cervus → cervo, but the glossary row records that at 17:34 the blind reader heard 'cervos' as 'servos' (homophones in Brazil) and 17:34 took 'corças'. Here the danger is greater: 'a voz do Senhor que prepara os servos' is a sentence a praying ear accepts at once, and nothing before it names an animal. 'corças' has no homophone; it loses the Latin's masculine (cervos) — the Greek ἐλάφους does not mark it. 'veados' (Matos Soares 1932) is a slur in Brazil. præparáre → preparar (καταρτιζομένου; Douay-Rheims 'prepareth the stags'): the Latin's verb, not explained.

reveláre: 'uncover, lay bare' (ἀποκαλύψει, 'strip bare'). The storm strips the thickets. The glossary's 'desvendar' is for eyes (118:18); 'descobrir' is heard in Brazil first as 'discover' (find), 'revelar' as disclosing a secret; 'desnudar' is 'lay bare', the sense, and plain. Douay-Rheims 'he will discover the thick woods' (the old sense of 'discover'); Matos Soares 1932 'descobre'. The future after the participle is the Latin's and is kept.

options.label: revelará
options.note: The cognate; heard as disclosing a secret.

decisions.why: condénsa: 'thick places, thickets'. The glossary row (117:27b 'in condénsis' → 'entre ramos densos') names 28:9. The Greek differs: here δρυμούς ('woods, thickets'), at 117:27b πυκάζουσιν ('thick-leaved boughs'), so by D15's test the two places need not share a word; 'ramos' would add a noun the Latin and the Greek lack here. 'matas cerradas' is the Brazilian collocation for dense woods. Douay-Rheims 'the thick woods'; Matos Soares 1932 'os lugares sombrios'.

decisions.latin: et in templo ejus omnes dicent glóriam
decisions.why: 'all will say glory' (πᾶς τις λέγει δόξαν): the Latin leaves open whether 'glóriam' is what they speak of or the word they cry. 'dirão glória' keeps both. Douay-Rheims supplies 'his' ('shall speak his glory'); Matos Soares 1932 'anunciarão a sua glória' (another verb). The Hebrew reads a cry ('all say, Glory!'); a colon and a capital would close the Latin's openness toward it.

options.label: dirão glória
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's two words, open both ways.

options.label: dirão: Glória!
options.note: The cry; closes the ambiguity toward the Hebrew's reading.

decisions.why: 'makes the flood to dwell' (κατοικιεῖ τὸν κατακλυσμόν): whether the flood dwells, or is made a dwelling, the Latin does not say. 'faz habitar o dilúvio' keeps the build and the doubt; 67:7a 'Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo' has the same causative (grep) and can follow it. Douay-Rheims 'maketh the flood to dwell'; Matos Soares 1932 'faz do dilúvio a sua habitação' decides for one reading.

options.label: faz do dilúvio a sua habitação

forms.diluvium: faz do dilúvio a sua habitação

decisions.latin: et sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum
decisions.why: 'Rex' is predicative: the Lord will sit (enthroned) as King. 'como Rei' supplies the particle Portuguese needs (Matos Soares 1932 'como rei'; Douay-Rheims 'shall sit king'). Rei capital, as 23:7 'o Rei da glória'. in ætérnum → para sempre (D23). The Vespers antiphon of the Dedication of a Church (Sancti/10-DU.txt) opens on this colon, 'Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum' (grep); the Portuguese opens on the Lord.

virtus (ἰσχύν) given by God to his people. The glossary gives God's virtus 'poder' (28:4 in this psalm: one noun, one word) and proposes 'vigor' for a man's own strength (21:16); here it is God's, given. 'força' is fortitúdo's. The Monday Lauds antiphon 'Dóminus dabit virtútem * et benedícet pópulo suo in pace' (Psalmi major.txt, Day1 Laudes2, grep).

decisions.latin: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace
decisions.why: benedícere God → man → bendizer (glossary, open; 133:3 'O Senhor te bendiga', 5:12b 'bendireis ao justo'). The Latin has the dative here ('pópulo suo'); Portuguese 'bendizer' takes the direct object in current use ('bendirá o seu povo'), and the colon then answers 28:11a ('dará … ao seu povo') without two datives running. in pace → em paz (glossary).

choices.28:1: The Latin's two 'sons' told apart by 'ó' (decision filii).
choices.28:2: glória et honor → glória e honra (glossary, 8:6); adoráre → adorar.
choices.28:3: majéstas → majestade (71:19 follows); intonáre → trovejar (17:14 'o Senhor trovejou'); aquæ multæ → muitas águas (Douay-Rheims 'many waters'), without article, as the Latin.
choices.28:5: The verse ends on ':' as the Latin; 28:6 continues it. Líbano is a proparoxytone at the cadence (a proper name, as the Latin's Líbani).
choices.28:6: Verbless second colon, as the Latin.
choices.28:7: commovére → abalar (decision concut). desértum Cades → o deserto de Cades. The one mediant of the Latin is kept; the third colon after the second ':' as the Latin.
choices.28:10: dilúvium → dilúvio (the Latin's word, the Flood; 31:6 'in dilúvio aquárum multárum').

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm28.txt, 10 prayed verses (no 28:8: DO joins the Greek's 7–8 in 28:7). No flex; one '*' per verse. No titulus (D7). Not in the Diurnal Monástico (a Matins psalm there; diurnal.py). Uses checked by grep in DO's Latin: Monday Lauds antiphons 'Deus majestátis * intónuit: afférte glóriam nómini ejus' and 'Dóminus dabit virtútem * et benedícet pópulo suo in pace' (Psalterium/Psalmi/Psalmi major.txt, Day1 Laudes1/2); the Dedication's Vespers antiphon 'Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace' (Sancti/10-DU.txt).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps028.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Repeats counted with ps005/grep_latin.py: 'vox Dómini' 7 times in 5 lines (28:3, 4 ×2, 5, 7 ×2, 9) — identical every time; afférte 4 in two lines, and 95:7–8 has the same formula and colon; 'fílii Dei' only here; intercídere, concútere, 'Cades', diléctus (substantive), 'sedébit' only here. Latin (= Greek) readings kept against the Hebrew: 28:1b 'filhos de carneiros' (the Hebrew doubles 'sons of God'), 28:6 'como a um bezerro do Líbano … o amado, como um filho de unicórnios' (Hebrew: Lebanon and Sirion skip like a calf, like a young wild ox), 28:7 'divide a chama' (not 'hews out'), 28:9 'prepara as corças' (not 'makes the hinds calve'), 28:10 'faz habitar o dilúvio'. To be tested by the readers: the seven verbless acclamations, 28:1 'ó filhos de Deus … filhos de carneiros', 28:9 'dirão glória', 28:10 'faz habitar o dilúvio', 'magnificência'.
